name: exec
description: Runs one executable with literal arguments, without an implicit shell. Inherits cwd and environment, receives EOF on stdin, and returns bounded stdout/stderr. Both program and args are required. Put only the executable in program and one argument per args element. For pipes or redirection, explicitly run /bin/sh with args ["-c", "the shell command"]. A tool status of success means execution was observed: check output.exit_code, output.signal and output.stderr. Exit code 0 means the program succeeded; nonzero or signal termination requires reviewing the diagnostic before correcting the call.

program.description: Executable name or path only. Put flags and arguments in args. A path itself may contain spaces. Use an explicit shell for pipes or redirection.

args.description: Required array of literal arguments, one element per argument, for example ["aux", "--sort=-%mem"]. Use [] for no arguments. For /bin/sh use ["-c", "complete shell command"].
